language.script_notes: Spanish as national; Quechua is widely spoken day-to-day and appears on cultural/tourism signage far more than on the coast — a strong regional tell alongside visible Indigenous dress and market culture.
false_friends: Bolivian altiplano (shares the same high-Andean landscape and Quechua/Aymara culture)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Black-and-yellow striped guardrails especially prominent on winding mountain roads.
road_furniture.line_paint: As national, though many roads are unpaved at higher/more remote altitudes.
road_furniture.curb_style: Cobbled streets in colonial Andean town centers (Cusco).
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national; dramatic switchback mountain roads common given the terrain.

architecture.roof_style: Red clay tile pitched roofs are the standard in colonial highland towns; some flat-roofed unfinished concrete construction as national default in expanding areas.
architecture.roof_material: Red clay tile is a strong regional tell in colonial towns, contrasting with the coast's flat concrete roofs.
architecture.wall_construction: Spanish colonial buildings built directly atop precise Inca stone foundations (most famously in Cusco) — massive, perfectly fitted stone blocks are a unique and unmistakable Peru/Andes tell; adobe construction common in smaller highland villages.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Whitewashed colonial upper stories atop dark grey Inca stone lower walls in Cusco; earthy adobe tones in rural villages.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Cusco's Spanish colonial buildings sitting on precisely cut Inca stone foundations; Machu Picchu and other Inca archaeological sites; red-tile-roofed colonial town centers; terraced hillside agriculture.

nature.vegetation: High-altitude puna grassland dominates above the tree line; cloud forest and terraced agriculture (potatoes, corn) on lower mountain slopes; eucalyptus (introduced) common around highland towns.
nature.terrain: Some of the highest mountains in the Andes, with deep valleys, dramatic peaks and high-altitude plains (puna); Cusco sits in a valley surrounded by mountains on all sides.
nature.climate_signature: Cold, thin, high-altitude air with intense sun and dramatic light; a visually rugged, mountainous look completely unlike the coast's flat desert or the Amazon's dense green jungle.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: As national; 4WD vehicles more common given mountain roads; llamas/alpacas visible alongside rural roads.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Good coverage around Cusco given its tourism importance; sparser in more remote highland villages.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Concentrated on the main tourist routes (Cusco, Sacred Valley, the road to Machu Picchu); real gaps in remote rural highlands.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shares the same high-Andean puna landscape, Quechua/Aymara cultural presence and Indigenous dress right across the border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Peru's guardrail stripe uses a black outer edge vs. Bolivia's yellow; Peru's Inca stone-foundation architecture (especially in Cusco) is distinctly Peruvian, and Peru's plates/road furniture differ from Bolivia's once compared directly.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The highlands are cold, mountainous, and culturally Quechua/Indigenous with Inca-stone architecture; the coast is flat barren desert, and the Amazon is dense green rainforest — all visually distinct.
